prerequisites: Competences corresponding to the first year of preparation for the license in Electromechanics.

learning_outcomes.text: Adequate application of knowledge on energy conversion, electromagnetic and mechanical phenomena specific to static, electromechanical converters, electrical equipment and electromechanical drives

Description of the operating principles of transformers, static and electromechanical converters, electrical equipment, the main sources of electromagnetic disturbances, as well as the rules on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of electrical and electronic equipment
Explanation and interpretation of operating modes of static, electromechanical converters, electrical and electromechanical equipment
To know the operating principles of static converters with switching operation
To explain and interpret the operating regimes of static converters
To study static converters using appropriate software (ORCAD, MULTISIM, SIMULINK)
To evaluate the results obtained from the simulations of static converters
Choose and use static converters in practical applications

syllabus_topics: Introduction. The role of electronic power circuits in industry. Application examples. Linear mode-switching mode comparison.
Analysis of the switching of power semiconductor devices. Power diodes, bipolar power transistors, thyristors, GTOs, triacs, MOS FETs, IGBTs, MCTs.
Converters a.c. –C.c. (rectifiers). The principle and general theory of phase-controlled rectifiers.
Single-phase rectifiers. Three-phase rectifiers. Control circuits.
Rectifiers with active power factor correction. Single-phase rectifier with boost type PFC circuit.
Static-like converters. Generalities. Principle of operation. Single-phase AC voltage converters.
Three-phase AC voltage converters. Direct frequency converters: cyclo-converters.
Direct frequency converters: matrix converters. Frequency converters with dc intermediate circuit. and bidirectional rectifiers.
DC converters - as single-phase. Classifications. Resonant inverters. Wiring diagrams. Waveforms. Applications.
Control methods of DC - AC converters. Frequency control. PWM command. Phase shift control. C-da by modulating pulse density.
DC converters - as three-phase. PWM control for three-phase inverters. Phasor modulation. Applications.
Converters c.c.-c.c. DC voltage sources made with the help of dc converters. - c.c. Buck type converters. Boost converters.
DC converters - DC buck boost type; Converters c.c.-c.c. tip Cûk, Sepic
DC-DC converters. with galvanic separation.
Presentation of the laboratory. Labor protection. General information on laboratory activity.
Control circuit for thyristors and triacs based on the dedicated circuit UAA145.
Single-phase rectifiers ordered using video projection
Study of single-phase alternating voltage variators.
Simulation of ac-dc, ac-ac converters using ORCAD.
Generation of PWM signals for the control of electronic power converters.
Study resonant inverters.
Modeling of series resonant inverters and their simulation.
Buck type converters with bidirectional switches.
Booster converters (step up).
Buck-boost converters.
Simulation of dc-dc converters using MULTISIM.
Study of fuzzy control converters with SIMULINK.
Closing the situation at laboratories. Recoveries.
teaching_methods: Explanations and discussions in the laboratory (including video projection)
Individual work for the preparation of laboratory reports and measurements on experimental assemblies
Using Orcad and Multisim simulation programs

assessment_methods.method: Activity during the semester + course reports
Tests to assess theoretical and applied knowledge during the semester
Final assessment test / Assessment by tests and online questionnaire for laboratory work

assessment_rules: The final mark is composed of 60% from the written exam, 10% from activity and course reports, and 30% from theoretical and practical knowledge acquired in laboratory. Obtaining a minimum grade of 5 in the laboratory gives the right to participate in the exam. For a grade of 5 in the course, students need to know the operation of main electronic power devices and static converters, and be able to analyze power structures. For a grade of 5 in the laboratory, students need to complete all laboratory work and reports, including measurements.
